candidates.source_name: CeJN - Centralni elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (portal home)
candidates.why_relevant: Single legally mandated national e-procurement system for Montenegro (live since 1 Jan 2021, built by Belit for the Ministry of Finance / Directorate for Public Procurement Policy with EU IPA funding). All stages - procurement plans, public calls, tender documentation, decisions, complaints, contracts and execution reports - must pass through it, so banking/payments-adjacent lots (POS terminals, card personalisation, payment gateways, cash handling, self-service kiosks, core banking/treasury software) surface here first and in full technical detail.
candidates.access_status: public browsing; registration required for economic operators to bid
candidates.legal_status: official government publication, public by law (Zakon o javnim nabavkama)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of the tenders listing with CPV/keyword filters; the portal is a JS/SPA-style app so a headless browser or its underlying JSON/XHR endpoints will be needed - server-side fetch of the root returned only the 'CeJN' shell, so plain HTML scraping is unlikely to work.
queries_used: cejn.gov.me portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora elektronske javne nabavke
Montenegro public procurement portal CEJN tender notices English
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch of https://cejn.gov.me/ and /tenders returned essentially only the string 'CeJN' - client-side rendered app, content not in initial HTML. Hypothesis, not a dead source.

candidates.source_name: CeJN - Tenderi (live tender notice listing)
candidates.why_relevant: The actual live notice feed of the national portal: open calls with deadlines, contracting authority, estimated value and downloadable tender documentation. This is the A2 spine - the first place a Montenegrin POS/payments/self-service/cash-handling lot becomes visible with specifications.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless-browser crawl or reverse-engineered API; filter by CPV families 30140000/30160000 (accounting & card machines), 48000000 (software), 66000000 (financial services), 79000000 (business services) plus keyword list; snapshot notice + attachment set at discovery time because documentation can be replaced mid-procedure.
queries_used: cejn.gov.me portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora elektronske javne nabavke
candidates.observed_blocker: Same SPA shell issue as portal root; treat as unverified rather than dead.

candidates.source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (Directorate for Public Procurement Policy, Ministry of Finance)
candidates.why_relevant: Policy owner and system operator behind CeJN. Publishes the legal framework, sub-regulations (pravilnici), registration instructions for economic operators, reform strategies/action plans and aggregate annual procurement reports. Essential for interpreting notice fields, thresholds, and for knowing which procedures are exempt from CeJN publication.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency crawl of news, 'propisi'/regulation and reports sections; PDF harvest of annual public procurement reports.
queries_used: ujn.gov.me Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki izvještaj planovi javnih nabavki Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: eTender Portal UJN CG (legacy pre-2021 notice archive)
candidates.why_relevant: The predecessor national notice portal (Delta 2015 platform) still exposes a free, unauthenticated notice search. Gives historical baseline of Montenegrin banking/payments procurement before the CeJN cut-over on 1 Jan 2021 - incumbent suppliers, prior award values, recurring contracting authorities.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off historical backfill via the noticeSearch form (GET/POST parameter sweep by year and keyword); note the documented quirk that '?' substitutes for diacritics (Š, Đ, Č, Ć, Ž) in search terms.
queries_used: portalujn.gov.me eTender portal obavještenja o javnim nabavkama pretraga

candidates.source_name: wapi.gov.me - Government of Montenegro document/file API
candidates.why_relevant: The shared file-delivery endpoint behind gov.me sites; tender documentation, draft pravilnici, commission decisions and ministry annexes are served from /download/{uuid}?version=1.0 and /download-preview/{uuid}. Useful both as a direct document fetch path and as a fingerprint for locating official PDFs indexed by search engines but not linked on portal front-ends.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Do not enumerate; resolve UUIDs from links found on gov.me/CeJN pages and from site-restricted search engine queries (site:wapi.gov.me + keyword).
candidates.discovered_via_method: observed in search results for tenderska dokumentacija
queries_used: cejn.gov.me javni poziv nabavka POS terminala platni promet tenderska dokumentacija

candidates.source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki - Rješenja (appeals decisions)
candidates.why_relevant: Appeal body for public procurement and PPP award procedures. Its published rješenja (decisions) reveal contested banking/payments tenders, the actual bidders and their objections, tailored technical specifications, and annulled/repeated procedures - often the richest competitive-intelligence text in the whole A2 workstream, richer than the notice itself.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the /rjesenja listing, PDF text extraction, keyword match on payments vocabulary and on known vendor names; cross-link decisions back to CeJN notice IDs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the appeals commission
queries_used: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki Crna Gora rješenja kzp.gov.me

candidates.source_name: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (State Audit Institution) - audit reports
candidates.why_relevant: Audits individual budget users and the procurement system itself, naming contracts, values, irregularities and suppliers. Its reports on bodies such as Uprava prihoda i carina and state agencies expose payments/IT contracts, direct awards and framework agreements that are hard to reconstruct from notices alone.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest from the reports section (/doc/ paths, URL-encoded Montenegrin filenames), full-text index, keyword match on payments/POS/IT vocabulary and vendor names.
queries_used: dri.co.me Državna revizorska institucija revizija javnih nabavki izvještaj Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: nabavke.com - regional procurement aggregator (Montenegro / CeJN mirror)
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial aggregator covering RS/ME/BA/MK/HR/SI that republishes Montenegrin CeJN notices AND rehosts the original tender documents under its own /tdoc-cejn/documents/ path. Extremely useful as a scrape-friendly, server-rendered fallback when CeJN's SPA blocks automated collection, and as a way to recover documents withdrawn from the official portal.
candidates.access_status: individual notice pages readable without login; freemium (15-day trial) for alerting/search features
candidates.legal_status: third-party republication of public data; site disclaims accuracy; check ToS before systematic scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Polite low-rate crawl of the Montenegro section as a secondary/verification feed; always treat CeJN as authoritative and nabavke.com as convenience mirror. Consider a paid subscription for legitimate alerting instead of scraping.

candidates.why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and the single most payments-relevant buyer in Montenegro (RTGS/instant payments, SEPA alignment, card/coin production, banking IT). It publishes its own tender and notice page in parallel to CeJN, sometimes with fuller technical annexes and with non-ZJN calls (design competitions, sale/lease notices) that never appear on the national portal.

candidates.source_name: World Bank Procurement Notices (Finances One) - Montenegro / TIPS Clone & SEPA project
candidates.why_relevant: The World Bank approved a EUR 8m loan (July 2025) for the Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization and SEPA Alignment (TIPS Clone) Project - instant payments infrastructure for CBCG. IFI-financed procurement runs under Bank rules and its notices/contract awards appear here (and in STEP), often BEFORE or instead of full publication on CeJN. This is the single most important non-CeJN channel for Montenegrin payments-infrastructure tenders.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Filtered pull by country=Montenegro via the Finances One dataset/API; monitor the TIPS Clone / financial infrastructure project id for General Procurement Notices, SPNs and contract awards.

negative_findings.description: No documented public API, open-data dump, RSS feed or bulk download for CeJN notices was found in this pass. Searches surfaced only the human-facing portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: cejn.gov.me appears to expose data only through its web UI; no /api, /opendata or RSS endpoint was documented in any source found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for A2 will likely require headless-browser rendering or reverse-engineering internal XHR endpoints, which raises cost and fragility; alternatively the nabavke.com mirror must carry the load.

negative_findings.description: WebFetch of https://cejn.gov.me/ and https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned only the token 'CeJN' with no navigation, filters, CPV taxonomy or notice URLs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Client-side rendered single-page application; server HTML contains no content. This is a rendering limitation, NOT evidence the site is down or dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The primary source of the entire cell could be wrongly scored as unreachable. Liveness and structure must be re-checked with a JS-capable fetcher before any conclusion.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searches for concrete Montenegrin banking/payments lots ('nabavka POS terminala', 'platni promet', 'tenderska dokumentacija') returned no live CeJN notice; results drifted to Bosnian (ejn.gov.ba) and Serbian portals.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero verified Montenegrin POS/payments tender notices retrieved via general web search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that CeJN notice bodies are not indexed by general search engines - discovery of payments lots must be done inside the portal's own search, not via Google-style querying.

negative_findings.description: The core local terms 'javne nabavke', 'portal javnih nabavki', 'tenderska dokumentacija', 'javni poziv' are shared across ME/RS/BA/HR and overwhelmingly return Serbian (jnportal.ujn.gov.rs) and Bosnian (ejn.gov.ba) results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Noisy terms identified; must be constrained with 'Crna Gora', 'Podgorica', 'cejn.gov.me', 'naručilac' + Montenegrin diacritic forms ('obavještenje', not 'obaveštenje').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Unconstrained local-language queries waste budget and risk ingesting foreign-jurisdiction notices into a Montenegro dataset.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language equivalents were found for CPV-style commodity vocabulary specific to payments hardware (e.g. an official local term list for 'card personalisation', 'payment gateway', 'self-service kiosk').
negative_findings.result_summary: Local vocabulary confirmed only for: POS terminal(i), platni promet, elektronska fiskalizacija, fiskalna kasa, eFaktura, elektronski sertifikat, bankarski softver. English-in-local terms (POS, gateway, kiosk) are likely used verbatim in specifications.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword filters must include untranslated English terms inside Montenegrin documents, or payments lots will be missed.

negative_findings.description: The appeals commission does NOT sit on the assumed kzp.gov.me domain; its decisions are published at kontrola-nabavki.me (contact komisija@nabavka.gov.me, Novaka Miloševa 28, Podgorica).
negative_findings.result_summary: Assumed domain wrong; correct domain identified and recorded as a candidate.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a false 'dead source' record and locates a high-value decision archive.

coverage_gaps.description: CeJN's internal search syntax, CPV taxonomy, notice URL pattern and pagination are unknown because the portal is JS-rendered and was not opened with a browser in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open cejn.gov.me/tenders in a headless/real browser, capture the XHR calls behind the notice list and notice detail views, and document field names, CPV filter values and stable notice URL patterns before building the collector.

coverage_gaps.description: Simple procurements (goods/services up to EUR 15,000; works up to EUR 30,000) bypass full CeJN procedures and appear only in contracting authorities' semi-annual reports - exactly the size band of many POS terminal, terminal-maintenance and small kiosk orders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a roster of payments-relevant contracting authorities (CBCG, Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond zdravstva, Fond PIO, Pošta CG, municipalities) and collect their polugodišnji izvještaji o jednostavnim nabavkama plus any local 'javne nabavke' pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Several likely payments-adjacent contracting authorities were reasoned about but not individually verified this pass: Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje, Fond PIO, Ministarstvo finansija/Državni trezor, Uprava za katastar, EPCG, Crnogorski elektrodistributivni sistem, Aerodromi Crne Gore, Luka Bar.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one targeted local-language search per authority ('<naziv> javne nabavke plan nabavki') and record each own-site procurement page as a separate candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Službeni list Crne Gore (official gazette) was not directly located or profiled, although it is the authoritative publication venue for the procurement law and its sub-regulations.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and profile sluzbenilist.me / the official gazette portal and add it as a pointer source for procurement-law and threshold changes.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage of award notices ('obavještenje o ishodu postupka') and signed contracts/annexes was only indirectly evidenced (a single CBCG award PDF mirrored on nabavke.com); the CeJN contract register was not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify the CeJN modules for decisions, contracts and contract-execution reports and confirm whether awarded values and supplier names are exposed in a listable form; if not, use DRI audits, kontrola-nabavki.me decisions and FOI as recovery routes.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed English-language interface for CeJN was found; UJN offers /en/ pages but the notice content itself is Montenegrin only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assume sr-only notice text; budget for machine translation and build the payments keyword list natively in Montenegrin plus verbatim English technical terms.

brief: Montenegro's A2 landscape has an unusually clean primary spine: since 1 January 2021 every stage of a public procurement - plan, javni poziv, tenderska dokumentacija, decisions, complaints and contracts - must run through CeJN (cejn.gov.me), the Belit-built, EU IPA-funded national e-procurement system operated by the Directorate for Public Procurement Policy (ujn.gov.me), with the pre-2021 record still searchable free of charge on the legacy eTender portal (portalujn.gov.me). The practical obstacle is not availability but machinability: CeJN is a JavaScript-rendered application with no discovered API, feed or bulk export, and its notice text is not indexed by general search engines, so payments lots cannot be found by web search - collection will need a headless browser or the commercial mirror nabavke.com, which rehosts CeJN tender documents under /tdoc-cejn/. Three material blind spots sit outside the portal: simple procurements below EUR 15,000 (many POS/terminal orders) that surface only in semi-annual authority reports; the Central Bank's own tenderi-i-oglasi page; and IFI-financed payments infrastructure - most notably the World Bank's July 2025 EUR 8m TIPS Clone / SEPA alignment project for CBCG, which will procure under Bank rules through Finances One and STEP rather than CeJN. Outcome and dispute detail is best recovered from the appeals commission's rjesenja at kontrola-nabavki.me and from State Audit Institution reports at dri.co.me.
